threads.body: [General] This makes `jvm.gc.cause` unconditional, but the current-behavior examples in `instrumentation/runtime-telemetry/library/README.md:223-253` still show every `jvm.gc.duration` point with only `jvm.gc.action` and `jvm.gc.name`. Those examples now misdescribe the emitted attribute set; update them to include representative `jvm.gc.cause` values (or explicitly state that the value varies by collection).

replies.body:
Addressed in 9034dcd652e221ede38ba3dad5150686e5d43a2b.

The README now states that every jvm.gc.duration point includes jvm.gc.cause and explicitly explains its omission from the six collector examples because the value varies by collection. Allocation Failure and System.gc() are representative values already asserted by GarbageCollectorTest. This addresses the inline finding and its duplicate overview without changing telemetry or collector-specific attributes.

threads.body: [General] This is only true for JMX-sourced GC metrics. When `jvm.gc.duration` is selected for JFR, the JFR handlers record only `jvm.gc.name` and `jvm.gc.action` (for example, `G1GarbageCollectionHandler.java:30-31,53`), so this sentence misdocuments a supported selector path. Scope the claim to JMX and clarify the JFR behavior.
